sources.citation: Nesfield, John C. 1883. The Kanjars of Upper India. Calcutta Review 77(154): 368-398.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic article; says only that 'Kanjars have adopted a secret language of their own, and use the vulgar tongue only when they speak to outsiders' (p. 368). No pronunciation or stress remarks in the scanned range checked.
Lists only Grierson 1922 pp. 95-102 as the descriptive reference (subclassification comment); alternative names Kagari, Kangar Bhat, Kangri, Kanjri. No phonological source.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1922. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. XI: Gipsy Languages. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Kanjari, pp. 95-102, specimens pp. 103ff., Standard List pp. 180ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress or accent in the Kanjari section (pp. 95-102: ethnography, sources, districts, noun inflexion, case suffixes, pronouns, verb conjugation, Dravidian element, peculiar words, word-disguising devices) or in the specimens. The only accent remark is the volume-wide transliteration note (the scanned text): the acute accent is used 'when it is necessary to mark an accented syllable', exemplified with Khowar; no acute accents appear in the Kanjari pages (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned textfinds none).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1922. Linguistic Survey of India XI: Gipsy Languages, Kanjari pp. 95-102 and Standard List pp. 180ff. — page-image scan (dsal.uchicago.edu / archive.org PDF)

sources.note: Already read in scanned; a page-image check would only confirm that no acute accent marks are printed in the Kanjari specimens and word list (scanned drops diacritics). Low value: the prose section contains no accent statement.

sources.citation: Kirkpatrick, W. 1911. A Vocabulary of the Pasi Boli or Argot of the Kunchbandiya Kanjars. Journal and Proceedings of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, N.S. 7(6): 277-287.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vocabulary with bibliography and ethnographic remarks; only says he tried to catch 'the real phonetic pronunciation' (p. 280). Acute accents in entries (Nimáni 'water', Bá pilo 'father') are Hunterian long-vowel marks, not stress. No stress statement.

sources.note: All entries are overview/ethnographic/wordlist types: Grierson 1922 (overview;comparative;wordlist;minimal), Nesfield 1883 (ethnographic;wordlist), Kirkpatrick 1911 (wordlist), Enthoven 1920-22, Narayana & Singh 2016 PLSI UP vol. 29(1) ('Nat aur Kanjar jati ki bhasha', overview;minimal, Hindi), Misra & Nagar 1990, Nagar & Misra 1989/1994, Mathur 1969, Fuchs 1969. Nothing on phonology beyond a paraphrase of Grierson's grammatical remarks; sources cited are Ethnologue, Grierson LSI, Frawley 2003, UNESCO atlas, Mhaiske et al. 2016 (none descriptive).
